implicit — own icon sheet alongside the basemap provider's, icons never appear,skills/maplibre-sprites-icons/SKILL.md,"My MapLibre GL JS style's sprite points at my basemap provider's URL. I host my own sheet of POI icons on my own domain, and I set icon-image on my symbol layer to one of my icon names. The basemap's own icons all render fine, but mine never appear and nothing logs an error. I'd rather not merge the two sheets or rebuild them. How do I get my symbol layers to reference the icons in my sheet?","## TL;DR
1. **Make the style understand that there are *two* sprite sheets** – the basemap’s sheet (the one that is already in the style) and *your* sheet that lives on your own domain.
2. **Reference the icons from your sheet with a prefix** (`my-icons:my-cafe`) in the `icon-image` property of the symbol layer.

3. Do this **without merging or rebuilding** the original sheet – either edit the style JSON once (preferred) or add the extra sheet at runtime with `map.addSprite()` (if you can’t touch the style file).
Everything else (CORS, correct URL format, MapLibre ≥ 3.0) stays the same.

column3: What MapLibre expects
One sprite sheet only. When the map looks for an image called `""my-cafe""` it searches **only** that sheet.

column2: You host a second sheet at `https://mydomain.com/sprites/poi` and set `icon-image: ""my-cafe""`
column3: The map never asks the second URL, so the image is “missing”. The console stays quiet because the style **does** contain an entry for `""my-cafe""` in the *second* sheet’s JSON, but that sheet was never loaded.

column1: The missing-image warning you see (`Image ""my-cafe"" could not be loaded`) only fires when the map *does* try to load an image that isn’t in any loaded sheet. Since the sheet never loads, the map never even asks for `""my-cafe""` → no warning.
## 2. The solution: **multiple sprite sheets** (MapLibre GL JS ≥ 3.0)
Since v3.0 the `sprite` property can be **an array of objects**:
* `id` is an arbitrary string you choose for the sheet.
* The **special id `default`** is the one that behaves like the old single-string form – its images are referenced **without a prefix**.
* All other sheets **must be referenced with the `id:` prefix** in any `icon-image` (or `*-pattern`) value.
### 2.1. Edit the style JSON (the cleanest way)
1. Open the style file (or the JSON you receive from the provider).
2. Replace the single-string `sprite` entry with the array shown above.
* Keep the basemap sheet as `id: ""default""` so all the existing `icon-image: ""cafe""` etc. keep working unchanged.
* Add your sheet with any id you like (`my-icons` in the example).
3. **Make sure the URLs are *extension-less*** – MapLibre will automatically request `.json`, `.png`, and the `@2x` variants.
4. Deploy the edited style (or serve it from your own domain) and point your map at that style.
### 2.2. Add the extra sheet *at runtime* (if you cannot edit the style file)
If the style is hosted somewhere you cannot change, you can still inject the second sheet **after the style has loaded**:
// 2️⃣ Wait until the sheet is ready (addSprite returns a Promise)
// 3️⃣ Now you can add a layer that references it
* `addSprite(id, url)` works exactly like the array form – the `url` is the **base URL** (no `.json`/`.png`).
* The `id` you pass here must match the prefix you use in `icon-image`.
* The call must happen **after** the style’s original sprite(s) have loaded (`style.load` or `load` event).
> **Tip:** If you later need to reference the same sheet from multiple layers, you only call `addSprite` once. Subsequent calls with the same `id` are ignored.
## 3. Checklist – everything that can still go wrong

* **Upgrade** – the array form is the official way forward and is supported in all current browsers.

It flags a MapLibre symbol layer as a route shield when layer.layout['text-anchor'] === undefined and layer.layout['symbol-placement'] === 'point'. It is tagging plain place-name layers as shields and skipping real shield layers. Is the heuristic sound, and what should it key off instead?","**Short answer:**

No – testing only for `layer.layout['text-anchor'] === undefined && layer.layout['symbol-placement'] === 'point'` is not a reliable way to recognise a *route-shield* layer. Many ordinary point-label layers (place-names, POIs, custom icons, etc.) have exactly the same two defaults, so they will be mis-identified as shields, while many shield layers do **not** meet those two conditions (they use a zoom-function or an expression for `symbol-placement`, they set `icon-text-fit`, they use a prefixed `icon-image`, etc.).
Below is a quick-reference of why the current heuristic fails and what you should look at instead.
## 1. Why the current heuristic is unsound

column5: Every point-label layer without an explicit `text-anchor` is flagged as a shield.

column4: “Exactly the string `'point'` → shield”.

## 2. What actually distinguishes a route-shield layer
A shield layer is a **symbol layer that combines two things**:
1. **A badge image** (the “shield” background) taken from the sprite sheet.
2. **A text label** that shows the route number (or name) on top of that badge.
The style expresses that combination in a fairly consistent way:

An **expression** that interpolates a *network* and a *ref-length* placeholder, e.g. `""{network}_{ref_length}""` or `[""concat"", [""get"",""network""], ""_"", [""get"",""ref_length""]]`.
When a style uses a *single* sprite sheet for shields, the ID may be prefixed (`my-icons:{network}_{ref_length}`) but the placeholder pattern stays.
column4: The placeholder tells the renderer to look up a *different* sprite for each length of the route number – that is the hallmark of a shield.

column1: **Bottom line:** The *only* property that reliably signals a shield is the **`icon-image` expression that contains a placeholder for `ref_length` (or a similar length-based token)** *and* a **`text-field` that pulls the route reference**. The other properties (icon-text-fit, symbol-placement, overlap) are strong supporting clues.
## 3. A practical heuristic you can implement
Below is a **minimal, high-precision** heuristic that works for the official OSM Bright / OSM Liberty styles and for most custom styles that follow the same pattern.
* Returns true if a layer looks like a route-shield layer.
* @param {object} layer – a style layer object (already parsed JSON)
// 2️⃣ Must have a text field that references the route reference
// 3️⃣ Must have an icon-image that contains a placeholder for length
// 4️⃣ (Optional but helpful) – check for icon-text-fit or a zoom-function placement
const hasFit = !!layout['icon-text-fit']; // true for stretchable badges
const placementIsFunction = typeof placement === 'object' && placement !== null && !Array.isArray(placement);
// If we have a fit or a non-default placement, we are even more confident.
// But we *don’t* reject the layer if they are missing – many shields omit them.

* **Prefix check** – if you know you are using a multi-sprite sheet, verify that the `icon-image` starts with the sheet id (`my-icons:`).
* **`id` name** – `layer.id.toLowerCase().includes('shield')` can be used as a cheap pre-filter before the more expensive checks.
